test_runs.scope: small synthetic rotation, artifact-order, administrator route, role-gate and indicator-evaluator tests only

validation_runs.command: .venv/bin/python -m py_compile src/facecheck/rotation_control.py src/facecheck/platform_api.py src/facecheck/platform_catalog.py scripts/evaluate_indicators.py tests/test_rotation_control.py tests/test_cloud_access.py tests/test_indicator_evaluation.py

checks: SQLite rotation plan and claim state is persistent
verified output is followed by transactional SQLite task pointer/manifest anchor/key metadata switch and audit event
interrupted worker can reuse a verified deterministic target
v1 migration re-encrypts data while v2 rewrap only replaces recipient envelope
feature cache cleanup and pending artifact gates are exercised
old task artifacts cannot be resolved before current task points at the target key
hidden staging entries and legacy rows without key_id fail closed
duplicate source key plans are rejected
administrator rotation routes enforce role checks and typed validation
indicator evaluator keeps rotation PARTIAL and global invalidation unproven
limitations: rewrap does not replace exposed per-video key material; compromise requires full data re-encryption
v1-to-v2 migration temporarily materializes plaintext in a restricted staging directory; forced termination can leave staging data
writer fencing, reader drain and external backup completeness are operator/deployment attestations, not cross-node enforcement
SQLite and object storage do not share an atomic transaction; deterministic target publication is a local saga recovery mechanism
no production KMS/HSM revocation or complete external backup/disaster-recovery inventory was exercised
scope_note: Small synthetic functional evidence only. It does not prove production key management, global revocation, scale, or 100 percent old-key invalidation. Formal recognition and throughput results are unchanged.
